newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian teachers say strike must go on.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian teachers say strike must go on.

text.p: Palestinian teachers said on Tuesday that a strike which has paralysed public sector schools in the West Bank must go on, despite the arrests of more than 25 colleagues.
Palestinian police made the arrests on Monday, among teachers who lead a strike in thousands of schools to demand higher wages and improved working conditions.
"The strike must go on and the Teachers' Coordination Committee will stand firm by its demand despite the arrests," said a statement from the group behind the strike.
Some 18,000 teachers began their strike at the start of April, in the first labour dispute involving Palestinian Authority employees.
"We demand the Palestinian Authority immediately release the teachers because their arrests are a rejection of their just and legitimate demands," the statement added.
The arrests highlighted internal divisions within the Teachers Union.

The Voice of Palestine Radio reported on Tuesday that the Teachers Union considered the Teachers Coordination Committee an illegal offshoot. Teachers said the Union leadership refused to back the strike.

PLO officials said Union representatives had promised Palestinian President Yasser Arafat that the strike was over and that the arrests were made after teachers were seen forcing students to leave their classes.

"We consider this an incitement against legitimate Palestinian institutions and a deliberate attempt to create chaos," Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, general secretary of the Palestinian presidency, told Palestine Television on Monday.
Teachers complain that they receive about 400 dollars a month which they say is not enough to cover basic needs.
Education Minister Yasser Amr told Voice of Palestine radio earlier this month his ministry had raised their salaries by up to 15 percent, but teachers said it was not enough.
The Jerusalem-based Palestinian Society for the Protection of Human Rights and the Environment called for the teachers to be released.
"Teachers have a right to union activity. Arresting and imprisoning teachers for labour union activities violates international law," a statement from the organisation said.
